While the dialogue is well-crafted and effectively uses subtext, the story relies heavily on very familiar, cliché romance tropes—such as estranged lovers meeting in a café on an autumn day, keeping a coat on to signal guardedness, ordering the exact same drink at the same time, and using impending rain as a metaphor for their mood. Because the characters and their conflict remain extremely vague, the story does not explore human nature deeply enough to offer the reader a unique viewpoint, new insight, or an original idea beyond the standard, well-worn theme of lingering feelings and missed opportunities.
